title: port
description: A contract: named operations, each with what it accepts and what it returns. A field marked static is fixed where the operation is called. A port a plugin grants is NATIVE (the plugin binds it); a port in a feature is a DOMAIN port (a binding binds it). Nodes run path#operation.

$schema.description: The kind of this document: its published schema URL, or the alias @wilanis/port.schema.json.

description.description: What this port is for, in one or two sentences: the capability, not its implementation.

label.description: A short human name for this document, shown wherever a reader sees it instead of its path. Absent: the file name stands in.

operations.description: The operations this port offers, by name: what each accepts, what it returns, and whether it is pure.

description.description: What this operation does, for a reader choosing between the port's operations.

accepts.description: What the operation takes: its fields by name, or the path of a shape whose fields it takes ("@customers/domain/CustomerUpdate.shape.json"), so a shape the operation takes whole is stated once. Either way a call site gives the fields under in one by one.

pure.description: True when running it changes nothing in the world. Native operations default to false.

refuses.description: True when running it ends the graph on purpose. Such an operation accepts a static `reason`: one word for the outcome (missing, conflict, upstream), which the trigger kind maps to how it answers. A rehearsal reports the node as refused on purpose.

holds.description: True when running it starts something that keeps running after the run has answered: a listener, a watcher, a subscription. Such an operation is named by a project's startup list, never by a graph; it answers what it started, and the runtime holds its teardown until the process stops.

transactional.description: True when running it can take part in the transaction of an atomic graph. Such an operation accepts a static field the checker resolves a connection from: `connection`, the path of a connection document, or `store`, the path of a store document that names one. A plugin grants it.

idempotent.description: True when calling it again with the same inputs changes nothing further. A string is an expression over the operation's accepted fields, in the grammar of a switch rule, that says when it is (method == 'GET'): the checker evaluates it over the literal inputs of each call site that retries. A pure operation never declares it; a domain operation declares true only, which its bindings are held to under every profile.

key.description: The accepted field the plugin recognises a repeated call by, so that a caller who gives it makes the call safe to repeat. Not written together with idempotent: one says the operation is repeatable as it is, the other how to make it so. A domain operation never declares it: the field belongs to the native operation its binding reaches.
